title: The stone that unlocked Egypt
text: The Rosetta Stone was unearthed in 1799, {{1}} Napoleon's soldiers were strengthening a fort near the Delta town of Rashid. The granite slab carries a single priestly decree written {{2}} three scripts: hieroglyphic, demotic and ancient Greek. The Greek text could be read at once, {{3}} meant scholars could attack the other two scripts by comparison. {{4}} took Jean-François Champollion until 1822 to announce his solution, and his breakthrough came fast once it came: Champollion, {{5}} command of the Coptic language descended from ancient Egyptian proved decisive, showed that the signs recorded sounds as well as ideas. The script {{6}} been silent for well over a millennium spoke again, and modern Egyptology was born {{7}} a single broken slab. Copies of its inscription were circulated {{8}} paper, so that scholars across Europe could race to be first.

gaps.explanation: Non-defining time clause after the year: 'in 1799, when…'.
'Written in' — the medium or script takes 'in'.
Sentential relative after the comma summarising the Greek discovery.
'It took someone until X to…' — the dummy subject of the time expression.
'Whose' shows possession: his command of the language.
Past perfect: the script had been silent before it spoke again.
'Born of' — the fixed phrase for origin.
'On paper' — the fixed phrase for the medium.
